title: Toward the summit
hook: two weeks to look back over five years and forward to a life
tomorrow: from the top of Nebo, what did Moses see that he'd never enter?

segments.voice: Six lines from your own path: your prayer, your text, your cause, your shabbat, your year, your rule of life. Yesterday, the whole Torah on one foot, and then: go and learn.

Hikers know the false summit: the ridge that looks like the top, and then there's more trail. This path has two weeks left. Noa leaves for college in about the same. Saba wants to walk her up the one real hill in their town before she goes, to look back at the houses. She'd rather pack. He's already waiting by the door with two bottles of water.
screen: `THE FALSE SUMMIT.` → `TWO WEEKS LEFT.` → `SABA, WAITING BY THE DOOR.`

segments.voice: There's a set of psalms with a heading that fits this walk: "A Song of Ascents." Tradition connects them with pilgrims going up to Jerusalem. One of them opens: "I will lift up mine eyes unto the mountains: from whence shall my help come?" And the next line answers: "My help cometh from the LORD, who made heaven and earth." The looking up is half of it. The other half is knowing where the help comes from on the way. Near the top of anything long, two things are true at once. You're nearly there. And the last stretch still has to be walked. So this is a day for looking back, without sorting: the words, the stories, the faces, the lines you kept and the ones you dropped. The next two weeks gather them up. Something to tell a friend tonight: the psalm about lifting your eyes to the mountains answers its own question in the very next line.
screen: `A SONG OF ASCENTS.` · `I WILL LIFT UP MINE EYES.` · `MY HELP COMETH FROM THE LORD.` · `NEARLY THERE, ONE STRETCH LEFT.` · then, large: `NEARLY THERE.`

segments.voice: Sit quietly, eyes closed, for the whole time. Let this path come back in no order: a word, a story, a face, one line you carried. Don't sort them or judge them; let each one pass, and notice which one stays.
screen: `EYES CLOSED.` · `LET IT COME BACK, IN NO ORDER.` · `NOTICE WHAT STAYS.`

segments.voice: Toward the summit: close to the top, looking back at the road, with one good stretch still to walk.
Here's the line: nearly there, with one good stretch to go. See you up the trail.
